title: Plots of posterior predictive checks for demonoid — plot.demonoid.ppc
text: Plot styles category. 40 styles fall seven   thematic groups. Styles whose name ends "Multivariate, C"   facet data column (one panel per series),   "Multivariate, R" variants facet row. Univariate predictive distributions. "Density" (default)   plots posterior predictive density yhat[Rows, ]   observed y[Rows] dashed reference line. "Density   Overlay" "Histogram Overlay" superimpose multiple replicated   datasets onto observed distribution. "ECDF"   "ECDF Overlay" empirical-cumulative analogues. Discrepancy goodness--fit. "Stat" (univariate test   statistic) "Stat 2D" (bivariate test statistics) compare   distribution user-supplied scalar function applied   replicated dataset statistic computed y.   "Jarque-Bera" "DW" (Durbin-Watson) compute classical   normality serial-correlation test statistics residuals,   respectively, multivariate column variants. "Mardia"   reports Mardia's multivariate skewness kurtosis. Fitted-vs-observed. "Fitted" plots posterior predictive   medians observed values 95% predictive intervals,   dashed 1:1 identity line, LOESS smoother, points coloured   absolute residual. "Fitted, Multivariate, C" produces one   panel per response column; "Fitted, Multivariate, R" per row.   "Scatter Average" plots posterior predictive mean   observed values, "Error Scatter" "Error   Histogram" display residuals. Residual diagnostics. "Residuals", "Residual   Density" "*, Multivariate, C" / "*, Multivariate,   R" variants render time-ordered residuals, residual densities,   per-series breakdowns. Predictive intervals counts. "Intervals" draws   caterpillar per-observation 50% 95% predictive intervals.   "Ribbon" stacks continuous ribbon ordered index.   "Bars", "Rootogram" "Predictive Quantiles"   target count outcomes (rootogram canonical PPC Poisson   negative binomial models). Covariate-aware checks. "Covariates" "Covariates,   Categorical DV" plot posterior predictive mean (per-class   probability) covariate column Data$X,   LOESS smoother. styles require Data covariate   matrix can retrieved. Spatial time-series checks. "Spatial"   "Spatial Uncertainty" require Data$longitude   Data$latitude (Data$X/Data$Y coordinates)   render posterior predictive mean width predictive   interval colour-coded site maps. "Space-Time Space"   "Space-Time Time" build analogous animations   ribbon-style spaghetti plot. "Time-Series" renders observed   replicated time series single panel; multivariate variants   facet series. forecast_start argument adds vertical   line separating -sample fit --sample forecast. Calibration. "LOO-PIT" computes leave-one-probability   integral transforms via PSIS importance weights renders ECDF   uniform reference, gold standard assessing whether   Bayesian predictive distribution calibrated. Grouped diagnostics. "Violin Grouped" requires   Group argument splits posterior predictive distribution   one violin per group, useful hierarchical models. Data requirements. styles strictly require   Data : "*, Multivariate, *" variants;   "Covariates", "Covariates, Categorical DV";   "Spatial", "Spatial Uncertainty";   "Space-Time Space", "Space-Time Time";   "Time-Series, Multivariate, C", "Time-Series,   Multivariate, R". remaining styles operate purely   y yhat stored x. "Fitted" family detail. "Fitted"   style multivariate variants workhorse visual   model criticism. render observed values x-axis   posterior predictive medians y-axis, vertical bars   spanning 2.5% 97.5% quantiles, points coloured   \(|\hat{y} - y_{obs}|\), dashed 1:1 identity line, LOESS   smoother colour. plot region forced equal-aspect via   coord_cartesian() deviation identity   geometrically meaningful, grey caption documents visual   encoding. "Fitted, Multivariate, C" requires Data$Y   produces one panel per series; "Fitted, Multivariate, R"   produces one panel per row.

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ## A simple linear regression with covariates set.seed(1) N <- 200; J <- 3 X <- cbind(1, matrix(rnorm(N * (J - 1)), N, J - 1)) beta_true <- c(1.0, 2.0, -0.5); sigma_true <- 0.7 y <- as.vector(X %*% beta_true + rnorm(N, 0, sigma_true))  Data <- list(y = y, X = X, N = N, J = J,              parm.names = c(paste0("beta[", 1:J, "]"), "sigma"),              mon.names = "LP") Model <- function(parm, Data) {     beta <- parm[1:Data$J]     sigma <- interval(parm[Data$J + 1], 1e-6, Inf)     parm[Data$J + 1] <- sigma     mu <- as.vector(Data$X %*% beta)     LL <- sum(dnorm(Data$y, mu, sigma, log = TRUE))     LP <- LL + sum(dnorm(beta, 0, 100, log = TRUE)) +         dhalfcauchy(sigma, 25, log = TRUE)     list(LP = LP, Dev = -2 * LL, Monitor = LP,          yhat = rnorm(Data$N, mu, sigma), parm = parm) } fit <- lucifer(Model, Data, c(rep(0, J), 1),                Iterations = 2000, Algorithm = "NUTS", Chains = 1) ppc <- predict(fit, Model = Model, Data = Data)  ## Default density plot of the first 16 records plot(ppc, Style = "Density", Rows = 1:16)  ## The full Fitted family: univariate, with 1:1 line, LOESS, and ## residual-magnitude colour gradient plot(ppc, Style = "Fitted")  ## Convenience wrappers ppc_dens_overlay(ppc)         # Style = "Density Overlay" ppc_stat(ppc, stat_fun = sd)  # Style = "Stat" with sd as test statistic  ## Aggregated PPC summaries plot(ppc, Style = "Density Overlay") plot(ppc, Style = "Intervals") plot(ppc, Style = "Ribbon")  ## Covariate-aware diagnostic plot(ppc, Style = "Covariates", Data = Data) } # }

title: Plot a directed acyclic graph — plot_dag
text: Input formats. formula argument accepts four   complementary input formats. Named lists formula lists provide   explicit control graph structure. Text/LaTeX notation lets   copy-paste mathematical model specifications directly papers   vignettes, LaTeX markup stripped automatically. Passing   lucifer Model function fitted demonoid object   triggers static analysis function body: parser identifies   parameter extractions parm[], distribution calls   (dnorm, dgamma, etc.), deterministic assignments   reconstruct DAG. Model parser works best standard   lucifer model structure (hyperparameters, priors, likelihood sections)   may miss edges models complex control flow unusual   coding patterns; cases, provide explicit edges via named   lists. Node types. function classifies nodes 7 types,   distinct visual encoding designed around three shape families.   data family (rectangles) includes data nodes   filled rounded rectangles deep navy missing nodes   dashed-border rectangles red. variable family (circles)   includes parameter nodes filled blue circles, latent   nodes dashed-border teal circles, hyperparameter nodes   smaller purple circles. distribution family   (ovals/ellipses) includes process_error green ellipses   obs_error orange ellipses. Edge styling follows greta convention: solid arrows   indicate deterministic relationships, dashed arrows indicate stochastic   relationships (sampling distribution). default, outgoing   edges distribution-like nodes (hyperparameter, obs_error,   process_error) rendered dashed. Auto-classification proceeds three layers: (1) topological,   terminal children become data terminal parents become   hyperparameter; (2) naming heuristics, regex patterns   node names override topology (e.g., sigma_obs maps   obs_error); (3) explicit node_types, take highest   priority. Plate notation. plates = TRUE, nodes enclosed   labeled grouping boxes. DiagrammeR backend uses native Graphviz   subgraph clusters (rendered dashed rectangles tinted backgrounds).   visNetwork backend draws plates via JavaScript canvas events. save static image, pass .html file path via   file. PNG/PDF conversion, open HTML browser   use screenshot tool, use webshot2 package.

title: Plot a directed acyclic graph — plot_dag
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # --- Format 1: named list of parent nodes --- plot_dag(list(y = c("beta", "sigma"),               beta = c("mu_beta", "tau_beta")))  # --- Format 2: list of R formulas --- plot_dag(list(y ~ beta + sigma, beta ~ mu_beta + tau_beta))  # --- Format 3: text/LaTeX notation --- # Plain text notation (one sampling statement per line) plot_dag("   y ~ Normal(mu, sigma)   mu ~ Normal(mu_0, sigma_0)   sigma ~ HalfCauchy(25)   mu_0 ~ Normal(0, 100)   sigma_0 ~ HalfCauchy(5) ")  # LaTeX notation (copy-pasted from a paper or vignette) plot_dag("   $$y_i \\sim \\mathcal{N}(\\mu, \\sigma^2)$$   $$\\mu \\sim \\mathcal{N}(\\mu_0, \\sigma_0^2)$$   $$\\sigma \\sim \\mathcal{HC}(25)$$   $$\\mu_0 \\sim \\mathcal{N}(0, 100)$$   $$\\sigma_0 \\sim \\mathcal{HC}(5)$$ ")  # Hierarchical model from LaTeX plot_dag("   y_i ~ Normal(theta_i, sigma)   theta_i ~ Normal(mu, tau)   mu ~ Normal(0, 100)   tau ~ HalfCauchy(25)   sigma ~ HalfCauchy(25) ", title = "Hierarchical normal")  # --- Format 4: lucifer Model function --- Model <- function(parm, Data) {     mu <- parm[1]     sigma <- interval(parm[2], 1e-100, Inf)     parm[2] <- sigma     mu.prior <- dnorm(mu, 0, 1000, log = TRUE)     sigma.prior <- dhalfcauchy(sigma, 25, log = TRUE)     LL <- sum(dnorm(Data$y, mu, sigma, log = TRUE))     LP <- LL + mu.prior + sigma.prior     Monitor <- LP     yhat <- rnorm(length(Data$y), mu, sigma)     return(list(LP = LP, Dev = -2 * LL, Monitor = Monitor,                 yhat = yhat, parm = parm)) } plot_dag(Model, title = "Normal model (auto-extracted)")  # From a fitted demonoid object # fit <- lucifer(Model, Data, ...) # plot_dag(fit)  # --- Customization options --- # State-space model with explicit node types plot_dag(   list(y = c("z", "sigma_obs"),        z = c("z_prev", "sigma_proc", "phi"),        phi = c("mu_phi", "tau_phi")),   node_types = c(y = "data", z = "latent", z_prev = "latent",                  sigma_obs = "obs_error", sigma_proc = "process_error"),   title = "State-space model" )  # Hierarchical model with custom plate groups plot_dag(   list(y_i = c("theta_i", "sigma"),        theta_i = c("mu", "tau"),        mu = c("mu_0", "sigma_0"),        tau = c("a_0", "b_0")),   groups = list("Observation" = c("y_i", "sigma"),                 "Group" = "theta_i",                 "Population" = c("mu", "tau"),                 "Hyperpriors" = c("mu_0", "sigma_0", "a_0", "b_0")),   title = "Hierarchical normal" )  # Interactive visNetwork backend plot_dag(list(y ~ beta + sigma), backend = "visnetwork")  # Disable Greek letter rendering plot_dag(list(y = c("beta", "sigma")), greek = FALSE)  # Hide legend plot_dag(list(y ~ beta + sigma), legend = FALSE)  # Save to file (multiple formats) plot_dag(list(y ~ beta + sigma), file = "dag.png") plot_dag(list(y ~ beta + sigma), file = "dag.pdf",          width = 800, height = 600) plot_dag(list(y ~ beta + sigma), file = "dag.svg") plot_dag(list(y ~ beta + sigma), file = "dag.html") } # }

text: function performs Bayesian missing-data visualization   data-augmentation framework. user fits lucifer model whose   parameter vector augmented one latent variable per   missing observation; lucifer's auto-FC Gibbs sampler (  inference engine) draws joint posterior parameters   imputations simultaneously. plot_imputed() extracts marginal   posterior imputed value, summarises requested   credible interval, overlays result observed time series. matching imputed parameter columns NA cells   data positional follows R's column-major ordering   matrices, convention adopted throughout lucifer (e.g.   .parm.names()). user follows convention   matching requires additional argument; otherwise   indicators argument can used provide explicit set   column indices. Style highlights different aspect posterior   imputation. "default" informative single view:   missing position carries vertical bar credible interval   hollow diamond median. "ribbon" converts bars   continuous band, makes contiguous gaps visually   prominent appropriate choice sensor dropouts   structured missingness. "draws" shows multiple posterior draws   simultaneously, reveals correlations across adjacent imputations   marginal credible intervals collapse away. multivariate input function facets series produces   self-contained subtitle reporting total counts observed   imputed cells across series. grey caption bottom-right   summarises visual encoding chosen Style.

title: Posterior imputation of missing time series observations — plot_imputed
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ## Univariate AR(1) with random missingness set.seed(42) n <- 120 phi <- 0.8; sigma <- 0.5 y_complete <- numeric(n) for (t in 2:n) y_complete[t] <- phi * y_complete[t - 1] + rnorm(1, 0, sigma) miss <- sort(sample(2:n, 25)) y_obs <- y_complete; y_obs[miss] <- NA  parm.names <- c("phi", "sigma", paste0("y_imp_", miss)) Data <- list(y_obs = y_obs, n = n, miss = miss, n_miss = length(miss),              parm.names = parm.names, mon.names = "LP",              pos.phi = 1, pos.sigma = 2, pos.imp = 3:length(parm.names)) Model <- function(parm, Data) {     phi <- parm[Data$pos.phi]     sigma <- interval(parm[Data$pos.sigma], 1e-100, Inf)     parm[Data$pos.sigma] <- sigma     y <- Data$y_obs; y[Data$miss] <- parm[Data$pos.imp]     LL <- sum(dnorm(y[-1], phi * y[-Data$n], sigma, log = TRUE))     LP <- LL + dnorm(phi, 0, 1, log = TRUE) +         dhalfcauchy(sigma, 5, log = TRUE)     list(LP = LP, Dev = -2 * LL, Monitor = LP,          yhat = c(0, phi * y[-Data$n] + rnorm(Data$n - 1, 0, sigma)),          parm = parm) } iv <- c(0.5, 0.5, rep(0, length(miss))) fit <- lucifer(Model, Data, iv, Iterations = 2000,                Algorithm = "Gibbs", Chains = 1)  ## Three styles plot_imputed(fit, data = y_obs)                          # default plot_imputed(fit, data = y_obs, Style = "ribbon") plot_imputed(fit, data = y_obs, Style = "draws", n_draws = 80)  ## With ground truth overlay plot_imputed(fit, data = y_obs, ground_truth = y_complete)  ## Multivariate: a 3-series VAR with missingness in two of the series Y <- cbind(y_complete,            y_complete + rnorm(n, 0, 0.3),            cumsum(rnorm(n, 0, 0.2))) Y[miss, 1] <- NA Y[sample(n, 15), 3] <- NA colnames(Y) <- c("temp", "humid", "pressure") ## Fit a multivariate model that imputes Y[i,j] for each NA cell, then: # plot_imputed(fit_mv, data = Y, Style = "ribbon", #              series_names = colnames(Y)) } # }

title: Profile likelihood curves from any lucifer fit — profile_likelihood
text: parameter \(\theta_j\), profile log-likelihood $$\ell_P(\theta_j) = \max_{\theta_{-j}} \ell(\theta_j, \theta_{-j})$$ \(\theta_{-j}\) denotes nuisance parameters. profile likelihood ratio \(R_P(\theta_j) = \ell_P(\theta_j) - \ell(\hat\theta)\) plotted \(\theta_j\), horizontal line \(-\chi^2_1(\alpha)/2\) threshold determining profile confidence interval [[1]](#ref1). univariate models (\(p = 1\)) nuisance optimization needed; profile equals log-likelihood evaluated directly grid. MLE standard errors extracted fit object via freq_summary internals. grid spans \(\hat\theta_j \pm 4 \cdot \mathrm{SE}_j\) n_grid points. Nuisance optimization uses stats::optim(method = "BFGS") starting full MLE. Profile confidence intervals reliable Wald intervals nonlinear models, boundary parameters, small samples, respect actual curvature likelihood surface rather approximating quadratic [[2]](#ref2).

what: Compute model weights via stacking or pseudo-BMA — stacking_weights
title: Compute model weights via stacking or pseudo-BMA — stacking_weights
text: Given two models pointwise predictive criteria (LOO, WAIC, K-fold, LFO), computes optimal combination weights. Stacking (Yao et al. 2018) maximizes combined log predictive density outperforms naive model selection models misspecified. Pseudo-BMA pseudo-BMA+ provide faster alternatives based information criterion differences.

title: Compute model weights via stacking or pseudo-BMA — stacking_weights
text: object class lucifer_stacking_weights, named   numeric vector model weights summing 1, additional   attributes storing method used.

title: Compute model weights via stacking or pseudo-BMA — stacking_weights
text: Stacking (Yao et al. 2018) finds weights \(w\)   maximize \(\sum_{=1}^N \log \sum_{k=1}^K w_k \exp(\mathrm{   elpd}_{ik})\) subject \(w_k \ge 0\) \(\sum w_k = 1\).   solved via stats::constrOptim(). Pseudo-BMA assigns weights proportional   \(\exp(\mathrm{elpd}_k)\) \(\mathrm{elpd}_k =   \sum_i \mathrm{elpd}_{ik}\). Pseudo-BMA+ incorporates Bayesian bootstrap uncertainty:   bootstrap weights drawn exponential distribution   applied pointwise elpd differences, yielding distribution   model rankings.

title: Compute model weights via stacking or pseudo-BMA — stacking_weights

text: function summarizes object class   pmc.ppc, consists posterior predictive checks   either \(\textbf{y}^{new}\)   \(\textbf{y}^{rep}\), depending respectively whether   unobserved instances \(\textbf{y}\) model sample   \(\textbf{y}\) used   predict.demonoid function. purpose posterior predictive check assess well   (poorly) model fits data, assess discrepancies   model data. information posterior   predictive checks, see   https://web.archive.org/web/20150215050702/http://www.bayesian-inference.com/posteriorpredictivechecks. \(\textbf{y}\) continuous known, function   estimates predictive concordance \(\textbf{y}\)   \(\textbf{y}^{rep}\) per Gelfand (1996),   predictive quantile (PQ), record-level outlier   detection used calculate Gelfand's predictive concordance. \(\textbf{y}\) categorical known, function   estimates record-level lift,   p(yhat[,] = y[]) / [p(y = j) / n], number   correctly predicted samples rate category   \(\textbf{y}\) vector \(\textbf{y}\). discrepancy measure approach studying discrepancies   model data (Gelman et al., 1996). Supported   discrepancy measures continuous y include:   "Chi-Square", "Chi-Square2", "Kurtosis",   "L-criterion", "MASE", "MSE", "PPL",   "Quadratic Loss", "Quadratic Utility", "RMSE",   "Skewness", "max(yhat[,]) > max(y)",   "mean(yhat[,]) > mean(y)", "mean(yhat[,] > d)",   "mean(yhat[,] > mean(y))", "min(yhat[,]) < min(y)",   "round(yhat[,]) = d", "sd(yhat[,]) > sd(y)".   categorical y: "p(yhat[,] != y[])".

title: lucifer 3.8.0
text: New BayesMode() function fully Bayesian inference number location modes distribution, implementing Sparse Finite Mixture (SFM) framework Cross, Hoogerheide, Ulker van Dijk (2024, Economics Letters) extended 11 distribution families. method fits mixture model via Gibbs MCMC sparsity-inducing Dirichlet hyperprior automatically prunes unnecessary components, detects modes fitted mixture MCMC draw produce posterior distribution mode count mode locations. result bayes_mode S3 object print(), summary(), plot() methods. C++ engine (src/mode_sfm.cpp, ~750 lines) implements family-specific Gibbs update steps 11 distributions: Normal, Skew-Normal, Student-t, Gamma, Log-Normal, Beta, Poisson, Shifted-Poisson, Negative Binomial, Geometric, Binomial. companion C++ file (src/mode_detect.cpp, ~400 lines) provides three mode detection algorithms: fixed-point iteration Normal mixtures (Carreira-Perpinán 2000), discrete enumeration count distributions, grid search golden-section refinement general continuous families. files support OpenMP parallelization. BayesMode() accepts raw numeric vectors lucifer posterior object (demonoid, laplace, iterquad, vb, pmc); given posterior object, returns bayes_mode_multi container per-parameter mode inference compact one-line-per-parameter summary table. print.bayes_mode() produces bayestestR-inspired pipe-separated tabular output showing posterior distribution mode count, P(multimodal), mode locations 95% credible intervals. summary.bayes_mode() adds MCMC diagnostics (ESS alpha, effective K, log-likelihood). plot.bayes_mode() provides six plot types: "modes" (data density posterior mode bands), "n_modes" (bar chart P(M modes)), "mixture" (fitted mixture density posterior draws), "trace" (MCMC diagnostics), "posterior" (violin plots mode locations), "convergence" (running mean diagnostics). family auto-detection logic selects Poisson non-negative integer data, Gamma positive continuous data, Normal general continuous data. Users can override family = "shifted_poisson" (11 families) tune sparsity prior via alpha.prior.

title: lucifer 3.8.0
text: Mode() Modes() now return objects class mode_estimate dedicated print(), summary(), plot() methods. return structure fully backward-compatible: Mode(x)[1], length(Modes(x)[[1]]), Modes(x)$modes work identically previous versions. functions gain method argument supporting four estimation strategies: "kde" (kernel density, existing default), "hsm" (half-sample mode; Bickel & Fruhwirth 2006), "venter" (Venter’s mode, shortest interval containing half data), "shorth" (shortest half-range). HSM Venter estimators C++ backends performance. summary.mode_estimate() compare = TRUE tabulates mode estimates across four methods. plot.mode_estimate() produces ggplot2 visualizations theme_relab(): "density" (default) overlays vertical mode markers kernel density curve, "histogram" marks modes histogram, "comparison" shows panel comparing four methods data. Added .print_pipe_table() reusable utility bayestestR-style pipe-separated tabular console output, used across new print methods.

text: lucifer() gains BurnIn argument gives user full control burn-(warmup) removal. NULL (default), BMK stationarity diagnostic estimates burn-boundary automatically . non-negative integer, many thinned samples discarded start, bypassing BMK entirely. returned object includes BurnIn.Method field ("user" "BMK") shown print() summary(). parameter threads Combine() multi-chain runs. Fixed critical degeneracy Posterior2 construction. BMK detected burn-(samples stationary), Posterior2 collapsed single-row vector instead equaling Posterior1. caused Summary2 DIC2 NA, predict.demonoid() fall back Posterior1 warning, LML estimation silently fail. Posterior2 now always proper matrix. BMK finds stationary region , first 50% samples discarded conservative fallback (warning) instead producing degenerate single-row result. Combine() gains BurnIn argument matching lucifer(), stationarity assessment mirrors fix: proper Posterior2 matrix, 50% fallback BMK fails.

Fixed crash (“subscript bounds”) pressing Esc twice parallel chain result collection. callr interrupt handler now catches secondary interrupts via interrupt = function(e) NULL inner tryCatch. Added stall detection parallel chain progress poller: chain shows progress 120 seconds, warning printed advising user press Esc. Replaced inline status printing print_status() six C++ samplers bypassing progress file mechanism: DEMC, AIES, twalk, DREAM (sampler_ensemble.cpp) HARM branches 2/4 (sampler_other.cpp). samplers now write progress callr polling file respond interrupt checks, fixing “0% -> done” progress display parallel runs. Added .write_progress() R-level flowMC NeuTra samplers.

IBIS mode prints analogous per-batch status. previous implementation printed stage %% Status intervals, adaptive schedules fewer 100 stages meant output ever shown.

Three Style options available. "default" draws vertical credible interval bars hollow diamonds missing position; "ribbon" converts per-position intervals continuous shaded band best suited structured contiguous missingness; "draws" overlays spaghetti posterior samples threading missing positions, revealing joint correlation structure nearby imputations marginal credible intervals collapse away. multivariate path facets series via facet_wrap(~ series, scales = "free_y"). grey caption bottom-right documents visual encoding chosen Style, subtitle reports count observed imputed cells missing fraction. title: lucifer 3.7.0
text: Exact transition density likelihoods Ornstein-Uhlenbeck, geometric Brownian motion, Cox-Ingersoll-Ross processes observation noise replaced affine Kalman filter implementations (loglik_ou_kalman, loglik_gbm_kalman, loglik_cir_kalman src/sde_engines.cpp). previous code used noisy observation y[k-1] proxy previous latent state transition density; observation noise present produces biased posteriors: kappa overestimated factor four obs_sd underestimated. new implementations track filtered state E[X_k | Y_{1:k}] via proper Kalman recursion. simulate.sde_model() now adds observation noise default (add.obs.noise = TRUE), correcting posterior predictive coverage approximately 91% 95%. EKF covariance update uses Joseph form P = (-KH)P(-KH)’ + KRK’ throughout; initial covariance changed 1e-6·1e-2·finite-difference step sqrt(machine_epsilon) optimal central-difference accuracy. new C++ function sde_filtered_states_exact_cpp() returns Kalman-filtered state estimates exact families. SDE() now warns Euler-Maruyama Milstein selected observation noise present. SDE trajectory prediction fixes. trajectory plot now uses Kalman-filtered state estimates via .filtered_posterior_paths(), achieving correlation observed data 0.97+ (previously near zero due unconditional forward simulation). predict.sde_fit double-simulation bug discarded x0 override second call; fixed. sde_simulate_exact_cpp now accepts optional x0 initial state start paths first observation rather stationary distribution.

title: lucifer 3.7.0
text: Multi-chain parallel execution responds Esc Ctrl+C gracefully: callr children receive SIGINT via handle$interrupt(), PSOCK workers check stop-signal file written C++ set_stop_signal_cpp()/clear_stop_signal_cpp(). grace period, parent collects whatever partial results available rather crashing. R-level MCMC samplers (Gibbs, GG, AGG, LSS, QSS, GPSS, NeuTra, flowMC, MCMCMC) cache partial state thinning points via .cache_partial()/.get_cached_partial() new R/interrupt_utils.R. VB methods return accumulated partial ELBO trace interrupt rather two-row zeros stub. PMC, LaplaceApproximation, IterativeQuadrature gain tryCatch(interrupt) wrappers. C++-level maybe_check_interrupt() function sampler_common.h uses std::chrono::steady_clock 200 ms intervals check user interrupts computation-intensive inner loops. output objects gain Interrupted field; print methods display warning banner results come interrupted run.

title: lucifer 3.7.0
text: algo_registry.R gains six new metadata fields per entry: multimodal_affinity, constraint_affinity, requires_torch, eval_cost_multiplier, dim_range, quality_tier. Algorithm subcategories corrected: Simulated Tempering, NRST, Wang-Landau, NRPT moved multimodal subcategory; BPS, Boomerang, ZigZag, Randomised HMC moved pdmp; Projected Langevin ProxMCMC moved constraint; NeuTra flowMC moved flow; Delayed Acceptance moved surrogate. Prescribe() replaces seven hard-coded MCMC scoring blocks unified .prescribe_mcmc_factors() dispatching 13 subcategories. Consort() Crucible() dispatch updated cover 82+ algorithms. New exported function algo_info() supports registry introspection filtering category, subcategory, gradient requirement.

title: lucifer 3.6.0
text: Three sampling algorithms multimodal posteriors added src/sampler_gradient.cpp. Simulated Tempering (Marinari & Parisi 1992): augmented state space temperature variable; Gibbs updates alternate parameter draw current temperature temperature transition proposal. NRST (Non-Reversible Simulated Tempering; Sakai & Hukushima 2016): deterministic even-odd sweep temperature levels direction variables, improving mixing relative reversible tempering. Wang-Landau (Wang & Landau 2001): flat-histogram adaptive estimation density states, converging uniform visits across temperature ladder.

title: lucifer 3.6.0
text: NeuTra (neural transport MCMC; Hoffman et al. 2019) reparameterises target via trained normalising flow, running standard HMC latent space geometry approximately Gaussian. flowMC (Gabrie et al. 2022) adapts flow online using MCMC samples, improving flow quality iteratively. R/normalizing_flow.R implements RealNVP module via torch nn_module methods. samplers implemented pure R tryCatch(interrupt) wrappers partial result recovery.

title: lucifer 3.6.0
text: coupling_diagnostic() added R/coupled_mcmc.R computes L-lag total variation upper bounds following Biswas, Jacob Vanetti (2019). function accepts two chains run common coupling kernel produces TV bound traces along meeting time statistics. S3 print plot methods included.

title: lucifer 3.6.0
text: Projected Langevin: Euler-Maruyama discretisation Langevin diffusion hard projection onto box simplex constraints step. ProxMCMC (Durmus et al. 2022): Moreau-Yosida envelope smoothing L1 total variation penalties, enabling gradient-based sampling non-smooth posteriors. implemented src/sampler_gradient.cpp.

title: lucifer 3.6.0
text: Relativistic MC (Lu, Niu, Lan & Liu 2017): replaces standard kinetic energy relativistic form, producing heavier-tailed momentum proposals improve exploration funnel-shaped posteriors. NR Overdamped Langevin (Duncan, Lelièvre & Pavliotis 2016): adds non-reversible antisymmetric perturbation overdamped Langevin diffusion, improving convergence rate without changing invariant distribution. GIST-NUTS (Bou-Rabee, Carpenter & Marsden 2024): iteration, K candidate step sizes drawn log-uniform grid; grid scored via softmax(−α|ΔH|) step size Gibbs-sampled resulting distribution; full NUTS tree built selected ε. design achieves approximately 87% acceptance rate compared approximately 70% standard NUTS test models. Total MCMC algorithm count Phases 51–58 additional proposals: 82.

title: lucifer 3.5.0
text: Three piecewise deterministic Markov process (PDMP) samplers added src/sampler_gradient.cpp. Bouncy Particle Sampler (Bouchard-Côté, Vollmer & Doucet 2018): velocity refreshment Poisson rate reflection equipotential boundaries, producing non-reversible continuous-time trajectory. Boomerang Sampler (Bierkens et al. 2020): replaces global reference measure Gaussian reference trajectory, achieving lower event rates log-concave targets. Randomised HMC (Bou-Rabee & Sanz-Serna 2017): stochastic trajectory length drawn uniformly [0, 2πL], breaking resonance artefacts fixed-length HMC.

title: lucifer 3.5.0
text: Three new slice samplers implemented pure R. QSS (Quantile Slice Sampler; Heiner et al. 2024): introduces unit-uniform auxiliary variable constructs proposals via quantile evaluations, reducing number likelihood evaluations compared standard stepping-. LSS (Latent Slice Sampler; Li & Walker 2023): augments target latent variable whose marginal characterises slice, enabling efficient sampling high dimensions. GPSS (Gibbsian Polar Slice Sampler; Biron-Lattes, Surjanovic, Campbell & Bouchard-Côté 2023): uses polar coordinates augmented space avoid difficulties anisotropic targets standard slice framework. three include tryCatch(interrupt) wrappers partial result recovery.

title: lucifer 3.4.0
text: Three samplers exploiting local curvature posterior added src/sampler_geometric.cpp (~400 lines) shared infrastructure src/metric_tensor.h src/metric_tensor.cpp. RMHMC (Riemannian Manifold HMC; Girolami & Calderhead 2011): uses position-dependent Fisher information metric via SoftAbs regularisation Hessian, adapting leapfrog geometry local curvature without divergences. LMC (Lagrangian Monte Carlo; Lan, Streets & Shahbaba 2015): casts dynamics Lagrangian system explicit velocity variables geometric integrator, producing sampler well-suited non-Euclidean target geometries. MHMC (Magnetic HMC; Tripuraneni, Rowland, Ghahramani & Turner 2017): adds antisymmetric component symplectic dynamics, breaking detailed balance locally preserving target invariant distribution improving mixing. Three metric modes supported: identity (standard HMC), Hessian (numerical Fisher information), SoftAbs (regularised absolute-value spectrum).

title: lucifer 3.4.0
text: Three gradient-based algorithms automatic step-size control appended src/sampler_gradient.cpp. autoMALA (Biron-Lattes, Surjanovic, Campbell & Bouchard-Côté 2024): searches locally optimal Metropolis-adjusted Langevin step size using geometric binary search, adapting local curvature iteration without global warm-phase. MALT (Metropolis Adjusted Langevin Trajectories; Riou-Durand & Vogrinc 2022): applies BAOAB operator splitting underdamped Langevin dynamics, combining mixing speed HMC momentum persistence SGLD. AAPS (Apogee--Apogee Path Sampler; Sherlock, Thiery & Vogrinc 2023): constructs HMC trajectories apogee apogee Hamiltonian, using multinomial trajectory sampling select next state.

title: lucifer 3.3.0
text: lucifer_threads() provides user-facing API thread budget management four strategies: auto (detect available cores distribute optimally), chains_only (threads chain-level parallelism, one OpenMP thread per chain), omp_only (threads intra-chain OpenMP operations), balanced (even split chain OpenMP parallelism). lucifer_parallel_info() produces diagnostic report covering platform type, core counts, OpenMP availability, platform-specific guidance. .lucifer_parallel_apply() cross-platform parallel dispatch helper using PSOCK clusters operating systems. .make_cluster() provides managed cluster creation. set_omp_threads_cpp() enables runtime OpenMP thread count adjustment R. inst/include/lucifer/thread_rng.h provides shared xoshiro256+ pseudo-random number generator header use across OpenMP regions C++ code, ensuring independent per-thread streams. SMC particle rejuvenation conditionally parallelised via OpenMP compiled models used. VB Pathfinder multi-path execution ABC rejection sampling now run parallel CPUs > 1. Critical fix: child chain processes previously OMP_NUM_THREADS hardcoded 1, eliminating OpenMP parallelism distribution evaluations, diagnostics, PSIS computations within chain. thread budget now inherited correctly parent process. SBI simulation via n_cores parameter Kfold cross-validation via CPUs parameter now work Windows PSOCK dispatch, replacing previous Unix-mclapply implementation. Explicit variable exports replace ls(.GlobalEnv) cluster export patterns across 14 files, eliminating source unpredictable failures. server_Listening(), legacy HPC socket server, deprecated. Use lucifer(Chains = n, CPUs = n) instead.

what: Neural ODE inference via Bayesian gradient matching
title: lucifer 3.2.0
text: NODE() implements neural ordinary differential equation inference following Bayesian gradient matching approach Bonnaffé (2023). sinusoidal observation network captures smooth temporal trajectories; dual-pathway single-layer perceptron process model approximates latent dynamics. BFGS optimisation OpenMP-parallelised ensemble fitting produces posterior ensemble neural network weights characterises uncertainty inferred dynamics. Geber criterion drives sparse network architecture selection; RK4 integration performs forward trajectory generation. C++ backend src/node_bngm.cpp (~620 lines, 8 exported functions) achieves approximately 0.2 seconds two-species Lotka-Volterra inference, compared approximately 5 minutes pure R reference implementation. NODE_predict() predict.node_fit() generate forward forecasts posterior ensemble. plot.node_fit() supports eight visualisation types: interpolation, dynamics, effects, contributions, network diagram, phase portrait, cross-validation performance, forecast.

title: lucifer 3.1.0
text: SBI() gains five new parameters. log_prior_fn accepts user-supplied exact log-prior function NLE NRE methods, eliminating multivariate Gaussian prior approximation used previously produced biased posteriors non-Gaussian prior shapes. max_grad_norm makes gradient clipping configurable (hardcoded 10.0). seed enables reproducible neural network initialisation. n_cores controls parallel simulation dispatch. pretrained_network enables warm-starting previously trained SBI network transfer learning sequential refinement. Three new diagnostic functions: C2ST() implements classifier two-sample test, trains binary classifier distinguish approximate exact posterior samples reports accuracy quality score (0.5 = perfect, 1.0 = maximally wrong). TARP() implements tests accuracy random points (Lemos et al. 2023), statistically powerful standard simulation-based calibration detecting posterior miscoverage. sbi_ppc() now exported direct use. Plot types "tarp" "c2st" added plot.sbi(). SBC() expected_coverage() extended NLE NRE via lightweight MCMC per calibration sample. NPE posterior sampling now uses rejection sampling within prior support, eliminating tail artefacts MDN density extrapolation outside prior. SNPE uses TSNPE truncation scheme IQR-based robust bounds, making immune heavy-tail bias outlier simulations. prior approximation uses full multivariate Gaussian including covariance structure support bounds, replacing previous independent normal marginals. Critical bug fixed: .sbi_eval_log_prior used environment() cache prior statistics, returned ephemeral execution environment rather model closure environment. cache never persisted calls, causing 10,000 prior draws generated every NLE NRE model evaluation.

title: lucifer 3.0.1

VB Salimans1, Salimans2, NGD infinite loop variance matrix V collapsed near-zero: (identical(xstar, m)) loop hang indefinitely Cholesky V produces zero displacements. loop now breaks 100 attempts noise-escape perturbation magnitude 1e-4. INCA crashed single-machine mode get("con") HPC socket connection objects absent; tryCatch fallback .hpc_mode flag now skips interchain serialisation non-HPC mode. Stochastic yhat (rnorm Model function) inflating sigma robust_influence.R approximately sqrt(2), making observations appear equally likely producing uniform PSIS importance weights; fixed via leave-one-log-likelihood decomposition: ll_i = total_LL - LL_{-}. BMK diagnostic gains NA guard Ind matrix small sample sizes.

title: lucifer 3.0.0
text: MCMC algorithm count increases 54 62. Barker Proposal (Livingstone & Zanella 2022): gradient-based proposals Barker balancing function, unique locally balanced proposal satisfying detailed balance Laplace increments; dual-averaging step-size adaptation targets 0.40 acceptance rate. Ensemble Slice Sampler / Zeus (Karamanis & Beutler 2021): gradient-free affine-invariant ensemble sampler using doubling-slice procedure; immune linear degeneracies highly effective correlated posteriors. DREAM (Vrugt, ter Braak, Diks, Robinson, Hyman & Higdon 2009): multi-pair differential evolution mutation, crossover, snooker updates; well-suited multi-modal high-dimensional problems. Non-Reversible Parallel Tempering (Syed, Bouchard-Côté, Deligiannidis & Doucet 2022): deterministic even-odd sweep replica ladder direction variables, outperforming reversible parallel tempering computational cost. Delayed Acceptance MCMC (Christen & Fox 2005): two-stage acceptance using cheap surrogate model pre-screen proposals, exact likelihood evaluated pre-accepted proposals; auto subset-data surrogate provided custom surrogate supplied. Zanella Locally Balanced (Zanella 2020): optimal discrete proposals via sqrt- min-balancing functions proposal weight; src/sampler_discrete.cpp new. Polya-Gamma Data Augmentation (Polson, Scott & Windle 2013): exact Gibbs sampler logistic binomial regression models via Polya-Gamma auxiliary variable augmentation, producing conjugate Gaussian updates regression coefficients. Zig-Zag Sampler (Bierkens, Fearnhead & Roberts 2019): piecewise deterministic Markov process componentwise velocity flips Poisson event times determined gradient log-target.

title: lucifer 2.6.0

title: lucifer 2.6.0

title: lucifer 2.4.0

WSABI-L (Gunter, Osborne, Garnett, Hennig & Roberts 2014) warps integrand square-root transformation linearises tractable GP updates. title: lucifer 2.2.0
text: VariationalBayes() now supports seven general-purpose variational inference algorithms via Method argument, single Salimans2 method. new methods span modern VI landscape fixed-form stochastic approximation particle-based inference. Salimans1 implements first algorithm Salimans Knowles (2013), using gradient information. precision matrix updated via outer product gradients, reducing per-iteration cost O(J²/2) O(J+1) model evaluations. ADVI.mf implements mean-field automatic differentiation variational inference (Kucukelbir et al. 2017) reparameterisation trick Adam optimisation. ADVI.fr full-rank variant, parameterising covariance lower-triangular Cholesky factor; warning issued J > 50. BBVI implements black-box variational inference (Ranganath et al. 2014) using score function estimator per-component control variate baselines. SVGD implements Stein variational gradient descent (Liu & Wang 2016), particle-based method updates K particles via functional gradient KL divergence reproducing kernel Hilbert space. NGD implements natural gradient variational inference (Amari 1998; Khan & Lin 2017) Robbins-Monro schedule. Shared infrastructure: numerically stable softplus sigmoid functions, Adam optimiser, .clip_grad() (max_norm = 10). Four bug fixes: reparameterisation trick longer overwrites theta model-evaluation parm, broke gradient consistency; Adam v-hat longer permanently corrupted gradient explosions constraint boundaries; false early convergence noisy ELBO prevented patience mechanism requiring 20 consecutive passes min_iter; LP < −1e100 initial parameter value now caught reported.

title: lucifer 2.1.0
text: LOO() computes approximate leave-one-cross-validation via Pareto smoothed importance sampling, following Vehtari, Gelman Gabry (2017) Vehtari, Simpson, Gelman, Yao Gabry (2024). function accepts N × S pointwise log-likelihood matrix WAIC() returns elpd_loo, p_loo, looic standard errors, plus per-observation Pareto k shape parameters diagnose reliability. GPD fitting uses Zhang Stephens (2009) method weakly informative prior adjustment. src/psis.cpp (~230 lines) parallelises observations via OpenMP. PSIS() provides standalone Pareto smoothed importance sampling general importance ratio stabilisation. print.loo displays LOO table Pareto k threshold counts. plot.loo produces ggplot2 scatter Pareto k values coloured reliability category. summary.demonoid print.demonoid report LOO-PSIS Monitor contains pointwise log-likelihoods.

what: Package renamed from LaplacesDemon to lucifer
title: lucifer 2.0.0
text: primary inference function renamed LaplacesDemon() lucifer(). LaplacesDemon.hpc() becomes lucifer.hpc() LaplacesDemon.RAM() becomes lucifer.RAM(). demonoid S3 class LaplaceApproximation() retain names backward compatibility.

title: lucifer 2.0.0
text: SDE() provides structured model specification stochastic dynamical systems. Users specify drift, diffusion, observation model, priors; package generates lucifer()-compatible Model function backed C++ likelihood engines. Four likelihood engines available: exact transition densities Ornstein-Uhlenbeck, geometric Brownian motion, Cox-Ingersoll-Ross, Vasicek processes; Euler-Maruyama discretisation general nonlinear SDEs; Milstein scheme higher-order correction; bootstrap particle filter producing unbiased log-marginal-likelihood estimates pseudo-marginal MCMC. Observation models include Gaussian, Poisson, binomial, user-defined likelihoods. Jump-diffusion processes supported via optional jump.rate jump.size arguments. Eight pre-built families provide convenience wrappers: sde_ou(), sde_gbm(), sde_cir(), sde_lotka_volterra(), sde_sir(), sde_fitzhugh_nagumo(), sde_merton(), sde_kou(). SDE.fit() bundles model specification MCMC inference, returning sde_fit S3 class trajectory, predictive, phase portrait, residuals, posterior, filtered state plot types. simulate.sde_model() provides forward simulation using exact transition densities Euler-Maruyama. New C++ files: src/sde_engines.cpp (~370 lines, 6 exported functions) src/particle_filter.cpp (~260 lines, 2 exported functions). SMC bug fixed: arma::vec returned C++ silently promoted 1-column matrix, causing cov.wt() fail “non-conformable arrays” tempering schedule jumped beta = 1 single stage.

what: Sequential Monte Carlo and Approximate Bayesian Computation
title: lucifer 1.4.0
text: SMC() implements adaptive tempering sequential Monte Carlo systematic resampling, random-walk Metropolis rejuvenation, online covariance adaptation. C++ backend src/smc.cpp handles resampling weight computation. ABC() implements approximate Bayesian computation three algorithms: rejection sampling, MCMC-ABC (Marjoram, Molitor, Plagnol & Tavaré 2003), SMC-ABC (Sisson, Fan & Tanaka 2007; Beaumont, Cornuet, Marin & Robert 2009). return S3 classes print, summary, plot methods. Four new MCMC algorithms added, bringing total 47. Stochastic gradient HMC (SGHMC; Chen, Fox & Guestrin 2014) extends SGLD momentum. Microcanonical HMC (MCHMC; Robnik, De Luca & Ramirez-Ruiz 2022) uses energy-conserving microcanonical ensemble. Dual-chain adaptive HMC (MEADS; Hoffman & Sountsov 2022) estimates mass matrix dual chains running parallel. Pseudo-marginal MCMC uses unbiased likelihood estimator (typically particle filter) noisy oracle, producing exact posterior samples intractable likelihoods. Two NUTS HMCDA bug fixes: momentum initialisation changed R::runif R::rnorm; dual-averaging now correctly accumulates alphaprime nalphaprime across tree-doubling iterations.

title: lucifer 1.3.0
text: Nine new distribution families added C++ implementations src/distributions_extended.cpp (~650 lines, 23 C++ functions) R wrappers R/distributions.R (~700 lines, 28 R functions). Tier 1 covers high-demand univariate distributions. ex-Gaussian (dexgaussian, pexgaussian, rexgaussian) models reaction-time data convolution normal exponential. von Mises (dvonmises, pvonmises, rvonmises) models circular data using Best-Fisher exact sampling algorithm. stable distribution (dstable, pstable, rstable) uses Chambers-Mallows-Stuck random generation numerical characteristic function inversion density evaluation. Tweedie (dtweedie, rtweedie) computed via Dunn-Smyth (2005) series expansion density compound Poisson-gamma simulation. Tier 2 covers copulas specialised distributions. Clayton (dclayton, rclayton), Gumbel (dgumbel.copula, rgumbel.copula), Frank (dfrank, rfrank) copulas dependence modelling; simplex distribution (dsimplex, rsimplex) bounded continuous data (0,1); matrix-t (dmatrixt, rmatrixt) matrix-variate heavy-tailed modelling. Tier 3 covers spatial distributions. intrinsic CAR prior (dicar, ricar) spatially structured random effects irregular lattices, using eigendecomposition-based pseudo-determinant computation. Matern correlation covariance functions (matern_corr, matern_cov) OpenMP-parallelised covariance matrix construction.

title: lucifer 1.2.0
text: lucifer() now accepts Grad argument gradient-based MCMC algorithms (HMC, AHMC, HMCDA, MALA, NUTS, Refractive, SGLD, THMC). Three modes supported: Grad = NULL (default) uses built-forward finite-difference approximation via partial_cpp; Grad = function(parm, Data) accepts user-supplied analytical gradient function validated startup; Grad = "numDeriv" wraps numDeriv::grad Richardson extrapolation higher-accuracy gradients adaptive step size. Non-gradient algorithms ignore Grad parameter. dispatch function compute_gradient() src/sampler_common.cpp routes C++ finite differences R gradient function depending mode. seven gradient-based C++ samplers accept Rcpp::Nullable<Rcpp::Function> GradFn parameter. gradient function forwarded multi-chain execution Chains > 1.

title: lucifer 1.1.0
text: Rhat() implements split R-hat (Vehtari, Gelman, Simpson, Betancourt & Gabry 2021) Blom rank-normalisation, dispatching vectors, matrices, lists, demonoid objects. ESS.bulk() computes rank-normalised bulk effective sample size. ESS.tail() computes folded rank-normalised tail ESS. MCSE.quantile() provides MCSE quantiles via Flegal Jones (2010) batch method sqrt cuberoot batch sizes. Divergence tracking added seven gradient-based C++ samplers (HMC, AHMC, HMCDA, MALA, NUTS, THMC, Refractive) using threshold |ΔH| > 10 nats. summary.demonoid() rewritten report divergence counts, split R-hat quality assessment (excellent, adequate, converged), bulk tail ESS, alongside standard ESS.

title: lucifer 1.0.1
text: Sixteen algorithmic correctness bugs corrected across specs_validation.R, postprocess.R, C++ samplers. B1: Gibbs algorithm assignment used == comparison instead <- assignment. B2: shadow variable scoping instead Specs mutation four locations CHARM/HARM/HMC validation. B3: orphaned -guard AHMC Specs validation body. B4: Posterior2 dimension drop without drop = FALSE postprocess.R. B5: floating-point equality HMC momentum reflection replaced std::abs() < 1e-14. B7: 17 unchecked inv_sympd calls distributions_multivariate.cpp gain two-argument form bool check eigendecomposition fallback. B8: division zero col_vars_cpp/row_vars_cpp n = 1. B9: cloglog NaN p = 1; logadd log(0) inputs nearly equal, fixed log1p. B10: as_inverse_cpp eigenvalue regularisation improved near-singular matrices. B11: random index bias ceil(runif) replaced floor(runif). B12: slice sampler upper stepping asymmetry corrected. B14: parallel chains -broad environment export scoped required objects. B15: Gelman diagnostic silent failure replaced warning. B16: Initial.Values matrix column count now validated. Gibbs--MWG fallback returns full name “Metropolis-within-Gibbs”. MALA defaults gain missing gamma parameter. specs_validation.R refactored 954-line cascading -else chain 735-line table-driven architecture five declarative registries 34 per-algorithm validators.

title: lucifer 1.0.0
text: Computationally intensive operations rewritten C++ via Rcpp RcppArmadillo C++17 OpenMP parallelisation multicore acceleration. src/matrices.cpp provides 13 matrix utility functions including is_positive_definite_cpp, as_positive_definite_cpp, as_symmetric_matrix_cpp, tr_cpp, as_parm_matrix_cpp, GaussHermiteQuadRule, Cov2Prec, Prec2Cov. src/math.cpp provides 8 mathematical functions: logit, invlogit, cloglog, invcloglog, interval, logadd, partial, softmax. src/distributions_multivariate.cpp (~580 lines, 44 exported functions) src/distributions_univariate.cpp (~540 lines, ~40 exported functions) cover density, distribution, quantile, random generation distribution families. OpenMP parallelises multivariate distribution evaluations observations. src/diagnostics.cpp (~330 lines) implements ESS via Levinson-Durbin AR fitting AIC order selection, MCSE (IMPS batch methods), IAT, BMK Hellinger distance via Gaussian KDE, OpenMP-parallelised posterior columns. MCMC sampler inner loops ported C++ across six source files organised family. src/sampler_metropolis.cpp: RWM, HARM, CHARM, OHSS, RSS, RDMH, SAMWG, SMWG. src/sampler_adaptive.cpp: , AMM, AMWG, AAMM, ASAMWG, ASMWG. src/sampler_gradient.cpp: HMC, AHMC, HMCDA, MALA, NUTS, THMC, Refractive. src/sampler_slice.cpp: Slice, UESS. src/sampler_ensemble.cpp: AIES, DEMC, twalk. src/sampler_other.cpp: AFSS, ESS, IM, MWG, ADMG, RAM. Nine algorithms remain pure R due inherent R-level dependencies: Gibbs, GG variants, AGG, SGLD, INCA, MCMCMC, RJ, USAMWG, USMWG. Shared infrastructure src/sampler_common.h src/sampler_common.cpp. package requires C++17 detects OpenMP availability automatically compile time.
